dossier.public_summary: The dip appears flat-bottomed but is not in the centre of the target star and is about 1.4 times longer than expected, and a secondary eclipse is seen. Difference imaging shows the signal is significantly off-target, pointing to an eclipsing binary on a nearby star rather than a planet around the M dwarf.

reasons.why: Difference imaging puts the dip 12.5" from the target at 4.9 sigma, not on the target, positively favouring a background/neighbour eclipse over a planet on the target
A second dip is seen at phasing expected for an eccentric stellar eclipse (not half-orbit 0.5/1.5), deep relative to the primary - stellar companion signature not planetary

Transit is 1.41x the central duration for this 0.3762 Rsun M dwarf, requiring an implausibly long eclipse - inconsistent with a central planetary transit and more typical of a blended eclipsing binary
ML planet likeness is very low, consistent with binary / blend checks
